title: Datadog: turn traces and monitors into an investigation
outcome: Connect Rails requests, jobs, SQL, and provider calls with useful service identity and bounded telemetry.
useCase: Investigating Rails/worker latency and release regressions.
drawbacks: Compatibility, sampling, volume, cost, and sensitive-data policy need ownership.
version: Pinned local examples · version-labelled configuration fragments
cue: Start from the symptom, then follow a traceable boundary.

trace.title: Service identity
trace.detail: Datadog combines observability capabilities such as infrastructure monitoring, APM, logs, and monitors. Choose the signals needed for a concrete investigation. Installing an agent alone does not make every request/job trace connected.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
User-visible latency spike → service latency/error metrics → slow trace → SQL or provider span → correlated safe logs → hypothesis → controlled repair → monitor recovery. Async boundaries need explicit context propagation/linking rather than assuming one synchronous stack.

An absent trace can mean sampling or missing instrumentation, not proof the request never ran.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Unbounded tags and full payload capture can create cost/privacy problems. A monitor without a clear action becomes noise. Trace instrumentation can be misconfigured even when infrastructure metrics arrive.
